neighbours.label: the companion in a shared social activity: the person one jokes, talks or walks with ('joking with me', 'talked with her', 'spoke with the old man'); the same verbs without a companion stay quiet
fire: On the bus home, she was laughing and joking with me about the exam.
During the break, he chatted with me for nearly an hour.
At the party, my uncle was teasing and joking with us all evening.
After dinner, the old farmer sat and talked with me on the porch.
The whole walk to school, Tom was joking with me about his dog.
My grandmother loves to gossip with me while she knits.
In the kitchen, the chef was laughing with me over a burnt pie.
Later that night, she argued with me about the film.
quiet: On the bus home, she was laughing quietly at a video on her phone.
During the break, he read the newspaper for nearly an hour.
At the party, my uncle was eating cake all evening.
After dinner, the old farmer sat alone on the porch.
The whole walk to school, Tom was thinking about his dog.
My grandmother loves to listen to the radio while she knits.
In the kitchen, the chef was scraping a burnt pie into the bin.
Later that night, she wrote a review of the film.
